item.text: I’m inspecting the workspace and the provided executable first so I can match the CLI and YAML behavior before writing the Node ESM modules.

I’ve confirmed the dataset is just this one script plus the compiled executable. Next I’m probing the executable’s CLI and YAML formatting edge cases so the Node version matches its observable behavior, not just the sample comments.

I’ve got the basic observable shape: scalars print with a trailing `...\n`, collections don’t. I’m checking a few invalid and structural cases now, because those affect both the parser and the dumper design.

I’ve confirmed PyYAML’s old YAML 1.1 scalar rules are in play, including `yes/no/on/off` booleans and octal integers like `0012 -> 10`. I’m now checking dump quoting and nested formatting, because those are the parts most likely to diverge from a naive implementation.
I’m narrowing this to a custom YAML 1.1 subset instead of a generic parser, but I need one more pass over scalar edge cases first: quoted-vs-plain strings, multiline strings, and a few numeric forms.

There are system-installed YAML packages already on the machine. I’m using them only as candidates to benchmark behavior; if one is close enough, I can vendor it into `/output` as local ESM and keep runtime imports strictly local.
